## Against QuantLib C++ {#sec-calendars-cpp}

The baseline of this chapter is QuantLib C++ itself. `tools/golden/p1_all_calendars.sh` built the v1.42 tag (commit `41b0e14`) from source, and that program wrote every calendar and market on every date from 1901-01-01 to 2199-12-31. The files in `tests/golden` hold its result: holidays on non-weekend days, business days on weekend days, and the dates where the calendar throws an error. The build is not repeated when this document is rendered. The joint and bespoke calendars in those files are left out, because the R package does not expose them.

```{r}
#| label: cpp-inputs
golden <- "../tests/golden"
markets <- read_csv(file.path(golden, "calendar_markets.csv"), comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) |>
  filter(!str_starts(key, "joint_|bespoke_"))
exceptions <- c("common", "americas", "asia_pacific", "europe", "middle_east_africa") |>
  map(\(region) read_csv(file.path(golden, paste0("calendar_all_", region, ".csv")), comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE)) |>
  list_rbind()
errors <- read_csv(file.path(golden, "calendar_all_errors.csv"), comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE)
serials <- 367:109574
all_dates <- as.Date(serials - 25569L)
day_of_week <- as.POSIXlt(all_dates)$wday + 1L
show_inputs(list(calendars = nrow(markets), from = min(all_dates), to = max(all_dates), dates_for_each_calendar = length(all_dates)))
```

RiemannFinMath, one call for each calendar:

```{r}
#| label: cpp-riemann
check_calendar <- function(name, weekend) {
  flags <- RiemannFinMath::is_business_day(name, all_dates, on_error = "na")
  weekend_days <- if (is.na(weekend)) integer() else as.integer(str_split_1(weekend, " "))
  is_weekend <- day_of_week %in% weekend_days
  expected <- exceptions |> filter(calendar == name)
  error_rows <- errors |> filter(calendar == name)
  error_serials <- map2(error_rows$first, error_rows$last, seq) |> list_c() |> as.integer()
  known <- !is.na(flags)
  tibble(
    calendar = name,
    holidays = length(setdiff(serials[known & !is_weekend & !flags], expected$serial[expected$kind == "H"])) +
      length(setdiff(expected$serial[expected$kind == "H"], serials[known & !is_weekend & !flags])),
    weekend_business_days = length(setdiff(serials[known & is_weekend & flags], expected$serial[expected$kind == "W"])) +
      length(setdiff(expected$serial[expected$kind == "W"], serials[known & is_weekend & flags])),
    error_dates = length(setdiff(serials[!known], error_serials)) + length(setdiff(error_serials, serials[!known]))
  )
}
calendar_results <- map2(markets$key, markets$weekend, check_calendar) |> list_rbind()
```

```{r}
#| label: cpp-results
bind_rows(
  judge_values(paste(calendar_results$calendar, "holidays"), "dates that differ", 0, calendar_results$holidays, "QuantLib C++ v1.42"),
  judge_values(paste(calendar_results$calendar, "weekend business days"), "dates that differ", 0, calendar_results$weekend_business_days, "QuantLib C++ v1.42"),
  judge_values(paste(calendar_results$calendar, "error dates"), "dates that differ", 0, calendar_results$error_dates, "QuantLib C++ v1.42")
) |>
  show_results()
```

The sections below use QuantLib's R package as a reference.

## Calendars

```{r}
#| label: calendar-inputs
pairs <- tribble(
  ~riemann_name,      ~quantlib_calendar,
  "japan",            list(QuantLib::Japan()),
  "target",           list(QuantLib::TARGET()),
  "us_sofr",          list(QuantLib::UnitedStates("SOFR")),
  "uk_exchange",      list(QuantLib::UnitedKingdom("Exchange")),
  "weekends_only",    list(QuantLib::WeekendsOnly())
)
from <- "2020-01-01"
to <- "2040-12-31"
show_inputs(list(calendars = pairs$riemann_name, from = from, to = to))
```

QuantLib:

```{r}
#| label: calendar-quantlib
quantlib_holidays <- function(calendar) {
  QuantLib::Calendar_holidayList(calendar, ql_date(from), ql_date(to), FALSE) |>
    ql_date_vector() |>
    map(ql_iso) |>
    list_c()
}
quantlib_lists <- map(pairs$quantlib_calendar, \(x) quantlib_holidays(x[[1]]))
```

RiemannFinMath:

```{r}
#| label: calendar-riemann
riemann_lists <- map(pairs$riemann_name, \(name) RiemannFinMath::holidays(name, from, to))
```

```{r}
#| label: calendar-results
pmap(list(pairs$riemann_name, quantlib_lists, riemann_lists), \(name, q, r) {
  compare_values(
    paste0(name, ": holidays only in one list"), "dates",
    0, length(setdiff(q, r)) + length(setdiff(r, q))
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  show_results()
```

Agreement here is agreement with QuantLib's rules, not with actual market holidays.

## Business days

```{r}
#| label: business-day-inputs
dates <- seq(as.Date("2026-01-01"), as.Date("2026-12-31"), by = "day")
show_inputs(list(calendar = "japan", from = min(dates), to = max(dates)))
```

```{r}
#| label: business-day-calls
quantlib_flags <- map_lgl(dates, \(d) QuantLib::Calendar_isBusinessDay(QuantLib::Japan(), ql_date(d)))
riemann_flags <- RiemannFinMath::is_business_day("japan", dates)
```

```{r}
#| label: business-day-results
compare_values("japan 2026: days that differ", "days", 0, sum(quantlib_flags != riemann_flags)) |>
  show_results()
```

## Differences of wrapper and core

```{r}
#| label: design
tribble(
  ~Layer,    ~Aspect,            ~QuantLib,                                        ~RiemannFinMath,
  "Wrapper", "Date argument",    "`Date` object made from day, month name, year",  "`Date` or ISO string",
  "Wrapper", "Calendar argument", "Constructor call such as `UnitedStates(\"SOFR\")`", "Name such as `\"us_sofr\"`",
  "Wrapper", "Date vector",      "Loop over a SWIG `DateVector`",                  "An R `Date` vector",
  "Core",    "Rules",            "Calendar classes with virtual `isBusinessDay`",  "Values and `match` over the same rules",
  "Core",    "State",            "None for calendars, except added holidays",      "None; added holidays do not exist"
) |>
  show_design()
```

The full calendar check is in the repository: every calendar of QuantLib C++ v1.42 was compared on every date (`docs/spec_dates_calendars.md`, section 3.5).
